nodes.name: NF pretreatment and phosphorization
nodes.procedure: NFs (2 cm × 3 cm) were degreased by sonication in HCl (3 M) solution for 20 min to remove surface oxides and then rinsed with acetone, ethanol, and isopropanol for 10 min, respectively. Finally, the NFs were dried at 60 °C in the ovens for 12 h. NaH₂PO₂·H₂O (3.0 g) was ground into powder and put in a quartz boat to mix with NFs evenly, and then set at the center of the tube furnace. The furnace was heated to 300°C (2°C min⁻¹) and kept for 2h under N₂ atmosphere. The obtained intermediate product (Ni₁₂P₅/Ni₂P nanorods) was used for next step.

nodes.name: Mo impregnation and sulfuration
nodes.procedure: The obtained intermediate product (Ni₁₂P₅) was immersed into MoCl₅ (0.1 M) ethanol solution for 1h and dried at room temperature, and then heated at 350°C for another 1h in N₂ atmosphere with sulfur powder supplied upstream. After that, the final product (Mo-NiPₓ/NiSᵧ) was obtained by centrifugation, after that washed with water and dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform Mo-NiS_x/NiP_y nanowires with nonuniform length 2-10 μm and diameter ~150 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: uniform Mo-NiS_x /NiP_y nanowires were obtained after subsequent impregnation and vulcanization (Figure 1a). The Mo-NiS_x /NiP_y nanowires exhibit a nonuniform length varied from 2 - 10 μm and a diameter of about 150 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanowire structure of NiP_x/NiS_y is maintained after Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we investigated the morphology of NiP_x / NiS_y without Mo incorporation. NiP_x/ NiS_y presents a nanowires structure, which proves the doping of Mo making little influence on the growth of hierarchical branched nanowires structure (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows heterogeneous nanostructure with inter-planar spacings: 0.204 nm for (202) Ni2S3, 0.158 nm (332), 0.216 nm (400), 0.234 nm (112) for Ni12P5, 0.202 nm (201), 0.221 nm (111) for Ni2P, and 0.198 nm for Ni17S18.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image further demonstrate heterogeneous nanostructure of as-prepared Mo-NiP_x /NiS_y nanowires (Figure 1b), in which the inter-planar spacing of 0.204 nm corresponds to the (2 0 2) facet of Ni2S3 species while the d-spacing of 0.158, 0.216, and 0.234 nm are indexed to the (3 3 2), (4 0 0), and (1 1 2) planes of Ni12P5 , in addition, the d-spacing of 0.202 and 0.221 nm correspond to the (2 0 1) and (1 1 1) facet of Ni2P , while the d-spacing of 0.198 nm corresponds to Ni17S18.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and elemental mapping show uniform distribution of P, S, Ni, and Mo throughout the entire Mo-NiP_x/NiS_y nanowire.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the composition information of the as-prepared Mo - NiP_x / NiS_y hetero-nanostructures was determined by high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) and corresponding elemental mapping measurements. The elements of P, S, Ni, and Mo are distributed uniformly throughout the entire Mo - NiP_x / NiS_y nanowire (Figure 1c-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD confirms crystal phases Ni12P5 (JCPDS 74-1381), Ni2P (JCPDS 74-1385), Ni3S2 (JCPDS 44-1418), and Ni17S18 (JCPDS 76-2306) in Mo-NiP_x/NiS_y catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal phase compositions of the Ni2P / Ni12P5 Ni3S2 NiP_x / SiS_y and Mo - NiP_x / SiS_y catalyst are determined by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern (Figures S3 and S4, Supporting Information). The diffraction peaks are corresponding to active species of Ni12P5 JCPDS No.74-1381), Ni2P JCPDS No. 74-1385), Ni3S2 JCPDS No. 44-1418), and Ni17S18 JCPDS No. 76-2306), respectively, indicating the successful synthesis of Mo - NiP_x / SiS_y hetero-nanostructures (Figure 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni, S, Mo, O, P elements; Ni 2p peaks at 856.53/874.5 eV (Ni2p3/2,1/2), 852.27/869.68 eV (metallic Ni), +1.2 eV shift after Mo doping; Mo 3d at 229.65/232.45 eV (Mo4+), 235.49 eV (Mo6+); S 2p at 161.75/162.84 eV with positive shift; P-O at 133.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further understand the chemical identity and detailed chemical and electronic states of Mo - NiP_x / SiS_y the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis is measured... High-resolution spectra of the Ni 2p, Mo 3d, P 2p, and S 2p were further characterized (Figure 2c-f).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows double-layer capacitance Cdl = 96 mF cm^{-2}, indicating largest ECSA among compared catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo - NiP_x / NiS_y electrode presents the largest C_dl value (96 mF cm^{-2}) compared to NF (2.9 mF cm^{-2}) , Ni3S2 (25.7 mF cm^{-2}) , NiP_x / NiS_y (41.4 mF cm^{-2}) , and Mo - Ni3S2 (71.4 mF cm^{-2})

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.5 Ω for Mo-NiP_x/NiS_y, indicating high electrical conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots analysis verify that the charge transferring resistance (R_ct) of Mo - NiP_x / NiS_y (0.5 Ω) is much smaller than pure NF (55 Ω) , Ni3S2 (4 Ω) , NiP_x / NiS_y (1.5 Ω) , and Mo - Ni3S2 (1 Ω) , suggesting a higher electrical conductivity of our hierarchical nanostructures in OER (Figure 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines optimal Mo/Ni mass ratio of 5.6% in Mo-NiP_x/NiS_y catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo - NiP_x / NiS_y electrode with Mo / N_i mass ratio of 5.6% exhibits the best oxygen evolution kinetics.
